key_insight: Dense user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes recoverable through dictionary learning.
engineering_relevance: This post-hoc, model-agnostic framework enables behavioral interpretation and natural-language audience retrieval without modifying upstream embedding systems.
method: Model user embeddings as sparse combinations of behavioral modes.
Recover modes with sparse dictionary learning, including sparse autoencoders.
Automatically name recovered modes and query them in natural language.
evidence_signal: SAEs outperform classical sparse baselines on synthetic ground-truth mode recovery, including transformer-encoded embeddings; real-world applications cover classical and transformer-based embeddings from two datasets.
watch_item: The behavioral-mode structure is only approximate for deep representations, so recovered modes and their natural-language labels require validation.
paper_title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
